messages:
maria: Hey team, hitting a customer issue for a Private (on-prem) deployment. Their inference nodes can't reach outbound Redwood endpoints. App logs show repeated 407 and timeout errors. No internet policy in place — they said only proxy egress is allowed. Can we triage?

support-bot: Thanks @maria — can you paste the exact error snippets and any repro steps the customer ran? Also request time window so we can check infra logs.

customer: Error from our side: 
`2025-11-16T09:12:03Z ERROR: request failed: 407 Proxy Authentication Required`
and sometimes:
`curl: (28) Connection timed out after 30001 milliseconds`
We followed the private quickstart (no-internet mode) and pointed REDWOOD_API_URL at the private control plane host.

alex: Two quick hypotheses: 1) corporate proxy requires NTLM/Negotiate and our client doesn't support it out of the box, leading to 407. 2) TLS interception (MITM) by the proxy means the control plane cert chain isn't trusted, causing curl/OpenSSL verify errors (you didn't paste cert errors yet).

jordan: Can the customer run a few small checks and paste outputs? Suggest commands: 
```
# DNS resolution
dig +short api.redwood.ai
# direct TLS handshake (bypassing app)
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai </dev/null 2>/dev/null | head -n 20
# curl via proxy (verbose)
curl -v -x http://proxy.company.local:3128 https://api.redwood.ai/health
# environment
env | grep -i proxy
```
Also ask them to try curl with `--proxy-user` if proxy needs basic auth.

customer: Running now. DNS resolves fine. `dig` returns our outbound proxy IP (so DNS is internal). `openssl s_client` returns a cert signed by our corp CA (not Redwood). Curl via proxy shows `* HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required` and `Proxy-agent: squid/4.13`. env shows `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY` set to `http://proxy.company.local:3128` and no NO_PROXY set.

maria: Good detail — corp CA MITM confirmed + 407. Next steps: 1) add corp CA to the system trust store on the nodes (or pass it to the Redwood runtime via `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` / `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`). 2) Ensure the proxy credentials method is supported by the runtime — if it's NTLM/Negotiate, you often need an auth helper (cntlm) or configure a proxy that accepts basic auth from internal service. 3) Set NO_PROXY for any internal control-plane hostnames and metadata IPs.

networking-sre: Also confirm firewall egress: ports 443/80 must be allowed to Redwood IP ranges if proxy bypass is used. If the customer must go through the proxy, ensure the proxy allowlist includes `api.redwood.ai` and `*.redwood-inference.com` (or whatever FQDN you use) and doesn't rewrite SNI. For NTLM: we recommend a local proxy-auth proxy (cntlm/ntlmaps) or using Kerberos-enabled clients.

alex: For quick repro/testing steps to unblock: 
1) Test curl with proxy and explicit credentials (replace placeholders):
`curl -v -x http://proxy.company.local:3128 --proxy-user 'DOMAIN\\user:password' https://api.redwood.ai/health`
2) If proxy is MITMing TLS, download their CA cert and test: `curl --cacert /tmp/corp-ca.pem https://api.redwood.ai/health`
3) If `openssl s_client` shows a corporate cert chain, add that CA to `/etc/ssl/certs/` (Debian) or the JVM/Java cacerts if components are Java-based.

customer: Tried `--cacert` and it succeeds. With `--proxy-user` we still get 407 unless using our AD credentials via negotiate. So it's NTLM. Installing cntlm locally and pointing HTTP_PROXY to `http://127.0.0.1:3129` worked in a quick test — our app can reach the health endpoint now.

jordan: Great find. For production, we should advise the customer on a stable solution: either configure a proxy mode that supports Basic auth from service accounts, or deploy a local authing proxy (cntlm/ntlm-proxy) on each inference subnet. Document steps: run cntlm with domain creds, point system HTTP(S)_PROXY to cntlm, add corp CA to truststore, set NO_PROXY for internal hosts.

maria: I'll draft a runbook snippet for them. Key checklist to include: 
- Determine proxy auth type (407 + Proxy-Agent indicates Squid/NTLM).
- If NTLM/Negotiate: deploy cntlm or use GSSAPI-capable client.
- Add corporate CA to OS and runtime truststores (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / CURL_CA_BUNDLE / JAVA cacerts).
- Ensure NO_PROXY contains control-plane hostnames and internal metadata IPs (169.254.169.254 if applicable).
- If possible, allowlist Redwood FQDNs at the proxy to avoid auth for service traffic.

support-bot: I've created ticket #SUP-8421 and linked this thread. @customer, once you confirm a stable config we can close. Anything else we should log (billing/latency impact)?

customer: Nothing billing-related. Latency improves once we bypass heavy proxy auth. We'll provision cntlm on a few nodes and update. Thanks for the guidance.

maria: Closing notes for the runbook that I'll paste to ticket: 
1) Example cntlm config snippet: 
```
Username    domain\\svc-account
Domain      MYDOM
Password    ********
Proxy       proxy.company.local:3128
Listen      127.0.0.1:3129
NoProxy     localhost,127.0.0.1,.company.local
```
2) curl test commands (repeatable): 
`curl -v -x http://127.0.0.1:3129 https://api.redwood.ai/health`
3) Add corp CA: `sudo cp corp-ca.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp-ca.crt && sudo update-ca-certificates`

networking-sre: Also add note about metrics: if you route through cntlm you may need to tune keepalive and connection pooling to prevent added latency.

maria: Thanks all — marking as resolved pending customer confirmation.
